It isn't cost effective going the reverse direction so no pressure on e.g. Ireland to open up pre-clearance in US airports as permitted under the treaty.    

Also entering such doesn't mean you are entering American territory, it is just that you are now in a restricted airport area (having passed immigration & custom checks that normally would occur in the USA).  It is still Irish territory - Irish law / Irish police / courts have full authority over that part of the airport terminal.
